column3: NASB supplies “Jesus” and renders “having come” as “after it has come.”
NASB has no “alone” after “by themselves.”
NASB follows the critical text without “as snow”; “shining” is rendered “radiant.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB omits “answering.”
NASB follows the critical text (“they became terrified”).
NASB follows the critical text; “there came a cloud” is rendered “a cloud formed.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “instructed” as “gave them orders” and “tell” as “relate.”
“Kept” is rendered “seized upon.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“He said”); “set at naught” is rendered “treated with contempt.”
NASB adds “indeed.”
NASB follows the critical text (“they came … they saw”) and adds “back” and “some.”
NASB follows the critical text (“saw … were amazed”).
NASB follows the critical text (“asked them”); “disputing” is rendered “discussing.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “possessed with” and “which makes him.”
NASB renders “throws down” as “slams him to the ground,” “is withering away” as “stiffens out,” and adds “at the mouth.”
“Until when” is rendered “how long,” and “bear with” is “put up with.”
NASB supplies “the boy” and “at the mouth.”
“How long a time” is rendered “How long has this been happening.”
NASB reorders the plea (“take pity on us and help us”).
NASB follows the critical text (“If You can?”), without “believe.”
NASB follows the critical text without “with tears” and “Lord.”
NASB renders “was running together” as “was rapidly gathering.”
NASB renders “as if dead” as “so much like a corpse” and “the many” as “most of them.”
Close to the Greek.
“Cast out” is rendered “drive out.”
NASB follows the critical text: “by prayer,” without “and fasting.”
Close to the Greek.
